info.title: Code Guard — security scan for AI-generated code
info.description: Code Guard is the in-loop check a coding agent runs on its OWN generated code/diff before committing. Deterministic rule engine (no LLM) for the high-frequency classes: command/code/SQL injection, SSRF, hardcoded secrets, weak crypto, unsafe deserialization, disabled TLS verification, XSS/template-injection, plus personal data left in source (email, US SSN, card number). Returns findings (rule, severity, line, fix) + a verdict (pass/review/block). LIMITS: 31 regex rules matched one line at a time. No parser, no data flow, no taint tracking, so this is not static analysis in the sense a SAST vendor means it. It produces false positives (the word DES on a line trips weak-cipher, comment or variable name included) and misses anything spelled differently, including a SQL concatenation split across two lines. Languages are JS/TS (11 rules) and Python (14 rules) plus 6 language-agnostic rules; there is no Go, Ruby, PHP, Java or Rust ruleset, and an unrecognised language value is ignored in favour of guessing from the source. A clean result means no rule matched, not that the code is safe.

post.summary: Match 31 regex security rules against a code snippet before committing/running it (JS/TS and Python; regex only, not full static analysis)

language.description: python | javascript | typescript (optional; auto-detected). Only JS/TS and Python are understood. Any other value is ignored and the language is guessed from the source.
